clue.text: Come to terms over the industrial action?

definitions.text: Come to terms over the industrial action?

parts.words: Come to terms over the industrial action?
parts.note: reads as settling a dispute about a walkout, and a deal struck in negotiation is exactly that, with a pun on the strike of industrial action

explanation.surface: Union and management settle their differences over a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for concluding a deal begins with the very word used for industrial action, so the whole clue describes it twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a deal through negotiation is to come to terms; the strike pun ties it to the walkout.

clue.text: Men in line went first and caused irritation

parts.note: a rank is a line of soldiers standing side by side
led, as a leader goes in front

explanation.surface: Soldiers on parade marched at the front and annoyed everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance that rankled kept irritating someone, a past-tense verb like the definition.

clue.text: Touch gently or collide

definitions.meaning: to brush with the lips, a light caress
in snooker or billiards, balls that touch lightly are said to do this

explanation.definitionFit: A light caress with the lips, and the snooker term for balls glancing off each other.

clue.text: Crafty trick by little Arthur provided on the rink

parts.note: Art is a short form of the name Arthur
if, as in provided that
a skating rink is made of ice

explanation.surface: A cunning move by a small boy named Arthur while skating.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is cunning deception, a clever stratagem.

clue.text: Theofficeofa news-vendor

parts.note: a newsagent is a news-vendor, and the office or business of any agent is named by adding a suffix to the word agent

explanation.surface: Where a newspaper seller does their business.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed with its first words run together: 'The office of a news-vendor'. A news agency also gathers and sells news, which is the second layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The business or office of an agent, here also a bureau supplying news to papers.

clue.text: Be successful and economical in use

definitions.meaning: to achieve great things, as in she will do well in life
said of something that lasts and stretches far, like a little paint covering much wall

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to achieve much success and, of a resource, to last and cover plenty.

clue.text: Where a thankless person might get a roasting

definitions.text: Where a thankless person might get a roasting

parts.words: Where a thankless person might get a roasting
parts.note: a roasting suggests being cooked over a fire, so the place is in the fireplace, and split differently the phrase names an ungrateful person

explanation.surface: A place an ungrateful person might be told off sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN GRATE it is where things roast in the fire; joined, it is a thankless person. 'Roasting' also means a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person is one who gives no thanks; the split reading is the fireplace location.

clue.text: Protest about another monster tax

indicators.note: another version of the word monster means its letters rearranged into a new form

parts.note: a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: Complaining about yet another enormous levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the anagram signal: another form of the monster. Rates were the old British local property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate about something is to object to it forcefully.

clue.text: Fresh taste in Oriental liqueur

indicators.note: a fresh arrangement of these letters means they are reworked into a new order

parts.note: E for East, Oriental meaning eastern

explanation.surface: A new flavour found in an Eastern drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges TASTE and IN into ANISETT, and E from 'Oriental' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Corner an early invader

definitions.meaning: the meeting point of two lines or walls, a nook
one of the Germanic peoples who settled in Britain in the fifth century

explanation.definitionFit: A corner is formed at the meeting of two lines; the Angles were early settlers who gave England its name.

clue.text: Keep tally of the best total yet

definitions.meaning: to write down the running count of points
the highest number of points ever achieved

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase, to note down the points; as a noun phrase, an all-time best tally.

clue.text: Girl model languished somewhat

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A young fashion model was rather listless.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a girl's first name.

clue.text: A football club catches one, then one more concerning fuss caused by a fan

indicators.note: a club that catches something holds it within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
another I, the Roman numeral for one
on, as in a talk on a subject
ado means bother or commotion

explanation.surface: A football club signs a player, then another, and a supporter makes a commotion about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catches' puts I inside FC to make FIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is a keen enthusiast or devotee of something.

clue.text: Love mental torture in wishing evil on others

indicators.note: torturing these words twists them out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Psychological torment in a love affair is spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means having ill will, desiring harm to people.

clue.text: Survey that maps out the artillery?

definitions.meaning: the national mapping agency of Great Britain bears this word before Survey

explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is Britain's official map-making body.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names Britain's mapping agency and also mounted guns and munitions.

clue.text: Way out of decapitating an African

indicators.note: cutting off the head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: an old, now offensive word for a Black African woman

explanation.surface: A grisly-sounding escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses a dated term now considered offensive; removing its first letter leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit or means of leaving.

clue.text: Separate duties in turn

indicators.note: giving the words a turn twists their letters into a different order

explanation.surface: Divide up the tasks, taking them one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' looks like 'one after another', but 'turn' is the anagram signal and 'in' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To disunite is to split apart or divide.

clue.text: Artful deceiver?

parts.note: reads as a crafty trickster, but recalls the pickpocket nicknamed the Artful in Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: A cunning cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Dawkins, the Artful Dodger, is the young pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodger is an evasive trickster, and the Dickens nickname links it to artful.

clue.text: Study it up in the Newcastle area, the hard part of one's teeth

definitions.text: the hard part of one's teeth

parts.note: a den is a private study or room

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: NE for the North East of England, where Newcastle lies

explanation.surface: Researching dental anatomy in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentine is the dense tissue beneath the enamel forming most of a tooth.

clue.text: I apply for a soft paste round the column

indicators.note: one piece goes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: plaster is a soft paste that hardens on walls

explanation.surface: Someone applying wet plaster around a pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column set into a wall.

clue.text: Paint I'm smearing on the drums

indicators.note: smearing these letters spreads them about into a different order

explanation.surface: A painter daubs colour onto the percussion instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums in an orchestra.

clue.text: Seats I rearranged forthe rest of the day

indicators.note: rearranged says the letters of these words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Chairs were moved about so everyone could rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is printed with 'for the' run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap taken in hot countries.

clue.text: Fault-finding Roman magistrate promises to pay

parts.note: a censor in ancient Rome kept the register and supervised public morals
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A carping official from ancient Rome pledges money.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorious means severely critical, quick to condemn.

clue.text: Send out for a period on the way back

indicators.note: going the way back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a time is a period, as in a time of plenty

explanation.surface: Dispatch something for a while during the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to discharge or give off.

clue.text: Girl having a drink first

indicators.note: first says the drink comes before the other piece

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A young woman has a quick drink before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Gina is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Rear lift

definitions.meaning: to bring up children or animals

explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to bring up: one by upbringing, the other by hoisting.

clue.text: Dangerously rash-could be deadly

definitions.meaning: liable to bring about one's own death

explanation.definitionFit: The word means recklessly self-destructive and also tending toward self-killing.

clue.text: A seventies person?

parts.note: seems to mean someone from the 1970s decade, but means a person aged between seventy and seventy-nine

explanation.surface: Someone who belongs to the 1970s.
explanation.walkthrough: The seventies are a decade of history, but also of a person's age.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in their seventies is aged seventy to seventy-nine.
